dialogue.context: Percakapan tentang kesulitan belajar bahasa asing dan pengalaman komunikasi lintas budaya

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I tried to be a bit afraid to say something I think like in the foreign language. I can be a lot more assertive and forceful in my own language.
lines.translation: Saya mencoba untuk tidak takut mengatakan sesuatu dalam bahasa asing. Saya bisa jauh lebih tegas dan percaya diri dalam bahasa saya sendiri.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.text: I feel really self-conscious if I speak another language, because everyone is listening and thinking I'm making mistakes all the time.
lines.translation: Saya merasa sangat malu jika berbicara bahasa lain, karena semua orang mendengarkan dan berpikir saya terus membuat kesalahan.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I love speaking other languages – I feel much more expressive than I do in my own language and my true personality comes out.
lines.translation: Saya suka berbicara bahasa lain – saya merasa jauh lebih ekspresif dibanding ketika menggunakan bahasa saya sendiri dan kepribadian asli saya keluar.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.text: When you travel, there's sometimes a language barrier but people can communicate through gestures and facial expressions. Body language allows you to show people that you don't understand.
lines.translation: Ketika kamu bepergian, terkadang ada hambatan bahasa tetapi orang bisa berkomunikasi melalui gerak tubuh dan ekspresi wajah. Bahasa tubuh memungkinkan kamu menunjukkan bahwa kamu tidak mengerti.

speakingLab.context: Simulasi percakapan dengan tutor Mr. Khoirul tentang pengalaman belajar bahasa asing dan komunikasi lintas budaya

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Hello! Today we're going to talk about language learning and communication. Have you ever experienced a communication breakdown when trying to speak a foreign language? Tell me about it.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, I have. When I visited Japan, I tried to ask for directions but my broken Japanese led to confusion. I couldn't make myself understood, so I had to use body language and gestures instead.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That's a great example! Body language can be very helpful. How do you feel different when you speak English compared to when you speak your first language? Are you more assertive or modest?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm usually a modest person when I speak my native language, but when I speak English, I feel a bit more self-conscious. However hard I try, I sometimes worry about making mistakes in front of others.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That's completely normal! Many language learners feel that way. What strategies do you use to overcome this language barrier? Do you think gestures and facial expressions help you communicate more expressively?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, definitely. I've found that body language, while obviously not words, can also be used to show people that I don't understand. It helps bridge the gap when words fail me.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence with the correct relative clause: 'They discovered three ancient scripts, ______ had been written by priests.'
options: all of which
which all
all of them
that all
quiz.explanation: Gunakan 'all of which' untuk merujuk pada keseluruhan kelompok benda (three ancient scripts). Pola: noun + comma + all/many/some of which/whom + verb.

quiz.question: Which expression correctly shows you didn't understand someone? 'I ______ what she was saying about the hieroglyphics.'
options: didn't quite catch
couldn't understand nothing
am not familiar
wasn't knowing
quiz.explanation: Untuk mengungkapkan ketidakpahaman dengan sopan, gunakan 'didn't quite catch' atau 'didn't quite get'. Ini lebih halus daripada langsung mengatakan 'didn't understand'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence using 'however': '______, they couldn't decipher the code.'
options: However hard they tried
However they tried hard
They tried however hard
Hard however they tried
quiz.explanation: Pola concessive dengan 'however' adalah: However + adjective/adverb + subject + verb. Artinya 'sekeras apapun mereka mencoba'. Tidak boleh 'however + subject + verb + adjective'.

quiz.question: What does 'communication breakdown' mean?
options: When people cannot understand each other due to language barriers
When a machine stops working during a conversation
When someone speaks too quietly
When the internet connection fails
quiz.answer: When people cannot understand each other due to language barriers
quiz.explanation: 'Communication breakdown' adalah kegagalan atau hambatan dalam berkomunikasi, biasanya karena perbedaan bahasa, sehingga pesan tidak tersampaikan dengan jelas.

quiz.question: Complete: 'I can't ______ in this foreign language.' (expressing inability to be understood)
options: make myself understood
understand myself
make understand me
be understanding
quiz.explanation: Ungkapan 'make myself understood' berarti 'membuat diri saya dipahami orang lain'. Ini adalah causative structure untuk menunjukkan kamu tidak bisa membuat orang lain mengerti maksudmu.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses a relative clause with a preposition? 'The language experts, ______, studied the Rosetta Stone.'
options: many of whom
many of them
whom many
which many
quiz.explanation: Gunakan 'many of whom' untuk merujuk pada sebagian dari kelompok orang (the language experts). 'Whom' digunakan untuk orang, sedangkan 'which' untuk benda.

modules.title: Unit 9: Fairness Matters: Justice, Ethics & Relative Structures
modules.objective: Mampu membahas isu keadilan dan etika menggunakan struktur relatif kompleks, inversion negatif, serta ungkapan impersonal dalam konteks akademis dan sosial

theory.summary: Unit ini membahas topik keadilan sosial dan kesalahan sistem hukum melalui kasus nyata seperti Sally Clark, Rubin Carter, dan Guildford Four. Dari sisi grammar, kamu akan menguasai negative inversion (pembalikan urutan subjek-verb setelah ekspresi negatif) yang membuat kalimat terdengar lebih formal dan dramatis, misalnya 'Never have I seen such injustice' atau 'Not only did she lose her freedom, but she also lost her children'. Struktur ini sangat penting untuk penulisan akademis, essay argumentatif, dan presentasi formal di level C2.
rules: Negative Inversion: Ketika kalimat diawali ekspresi negatif (never, not only, no sooner, under no circumstances, rarely, seldom), gunakan inversi auxiliary verb + subject. Contoh: 'Never have I read about such disturbing cases' atau 'Not only were they convicted, but they also spent years in prison'

Negative Inversion dengan modal: Under no circumstances + modal + subject + verb. Contoh: 'Under no circumstances could they have committed the crime' atau 'Rarely can we see such miscarriages of justice'
Inversion setelah 'only': Only + time/condition + auxiliary + subject + verb. Contoh: 'Only after 18 years was he released' atau 'Only when new evidence emerged did they reopen the case'
Bentuk formal tanpa negative: No sooner + had + subject + past participle + than. Contoh: 'No sooner had the film finished than we left' atau 'Barely had they arrived when the police arrested them'

commonTrap.trapTitle: Kesalahan Urutan Kata dalam Negative Inversion
commonTrap.explanation: Pemula sering lupa membalik urutan subjek dan auxiliary verb setelah ekspresi negatif, atau malah menggunakan bentuk normal. Ingat: setelah kata negatif di awal kalimat, gunakan pola pertanyaan (auxiliary + subject), bukan pola pernyataan biasa
commonTrap.wrong: Never I have seen such injustice. / Not only they were innocent but they also were tortured.
commonTrap.correct: Never have I seen such injustice. / Not only were they innocent, but they were also tortured.

readinessQuestions.prompt: Manakah kalimat bahasa Inggris berikut yang menerapkan negative inversion (pembalikan subjek-auxiliary setelah ekspresi negatif) dengan benar?
options: Not only were they convicted, but they also spent years in prison.
Not only they were convicted, but they also spent years in prison.
Not only they had been convicted, but also they spent years in prison.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Dalam negative inversion, setelah ekspresi negatif seperti 'Not only' di awal kalimat, urutan kata harus dibalik menjadi pola pertanyaan: auxiliary verb + subject. Jadi 'Not only were they convicted...' adalah bentuk yang benar, bukan 'Not only they were...' yang menggunakan urutan pernyataan biasa.

readinessQuestions.prompt: Kesalahan umum dalam negative inversion adalah lupa membalik urutan subjek dan auxiliary verb. Manakah kalimat berikut yang menggunakan negative inversion dengan urutan kata yang BENAR?
options: Rarely can we see such miscarriages of justice in a democratic society.
Under no circumstances they could have committed the crime without being noticed.
Never I have read about such a disturbing case of wrongful imprisonment.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Kalimat pertama benar karena setelah 'Rarely' urutan kata dibalik menjadi 'can we' (auxiliary + subject). Opsi kedua salah karena seharusnya 'Under no circumstances could they have committed...'. Opsi ketiga salah karena seharusnya 'Never have I read...' — auxiliary 'have' harus mendahului subjek 'I'.

readinessQuestions.prompt:
Perhatikan percakapan berikut tentang ketidakadilan dalam sistem hukum. Isilah bagian [...] dengan respons yang paling tepat dan natural.

Steve: "He stole millions and left over 100 people jobless, but he only got a five-year sentence!"
Michelle: "[...]"
options: Only when you look at it that way does it seem truly outrageous — he could afford the best lawyers, and that made all the difference.
Only when you look at it that way it seems truly outrageous — he could afford the best lawyers, and that made all the difference.
When only you look at it that way does it seem truly outrageous — he could afford the best lawyers, and that made all the difference.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Opsi pertama benar karena menggunakan pola 'Only when + clause + auxiliary + subject + verb' dengan tepat: 'Only when you look at it that way does it seem...'. Opsi kedua salah karena tidak membalik urutan subjek-auxiliary setelah 'Only when' di awal kalimat. Opsi ketiga salah karena posisi 'only' harus di awal sebelum 'when', bukan setelahnya.

vocab.meaning: kesalahan sistem peradilan yang menyebabkan orang tidak bersalah dipenjara
vocab.collocation: Sally Clark was a victim of a terrible miscarriage of justice when she was wrongly convicted of murdering her two sons

vocab.meaning: menarik kembali pengakuan (karena dipaksa atau salah)
vocab.collocation: All four of them confessed under police interrogation but later retracted their confessions in court

vocab.meaning: memberikan kesaksian di pengadilan
vocab.collocation: One doctor gave evidence that caused Sally Clark to be convicted, but his testimony was later proven false

vocab.meaning: mengajukan banding atas putusan pengadilan
vocab.collocation: She appealed the verdict multiple times before finally being released from prison

vocab.meaning: menyembunyikan bukti (secara sengaja)
vocab.collocation: The prosecution withheld evidence that proved Conlon had been in London at the time of the bombing

vocab.meaning: ketidaksetaraan, kesenjangan sosial
vocab.collocation: The book shows that inequality depends entirely on the high murder rate in the US

vocab.meaning: kekurangan gizi, tidak diberi makan cukup
vocab.collocation: We live in an underfed society with a widening gap between the richest and the poorest

vocab.meaning: saksi mata dalam perkara hukum
vocab.collocation: A witness who was at the scene of the crime later came forward with new information

dialogue.context: Percakapan antara Steve (wartawan) dan Michelle (direktur perusahaan) tentang kasus korupsi direktur yang mencuri uang perusahaan dan menerima hukuman penjara 5 tahun

lines.speaker: Steve
lines.text: This makes me really angry. It's just so completely unfair! Only five years? After what he did?
lines.translation: Ini membuat saya sangat marah. Ini benar-benar tidak adil! Hanya lima tahun? Setelah apa yang dia lakukan?

lines.speaker: Michelle
lines.text: Well, when you put it like that, it does seem really bad. It's not unusual though for bosses like this.
lines.translation: Ya, kalau kamu bilang seperti itu, memang terdengar sangat buruk. Tapi ini tidak jarang terjadi pada bos-bos seperti dia.

lines.speaker: Steve
lines.text: Look it! Stole! And he's been found guilty. But he only got a five-year sentence. Apparently, he took loads of money over a long time and left over 100 people with no jobs for the future.
lines.translation: Lihat! Mencuri! Dan dia sudah terbukti bersalah. Tapi dia hanya mendapat hukuman lima tahun. Katanya, dia mengambil banyak uang dalam waktu lama dan membuat lebih dari 100 orang kehilangan pekerjaan.

lines.speaker: Michelle
lines.text: Yes. And you know, I think maybe he didn't get a more severe sentence because he's rich and could afford the best lawyers. That happens quite a lot of the time.
lines.translation: Benar. Dan kamu tahu, saya pikir mungkin dia tidak mendapat hukuman lebih berat karena dia kaya dan mampu membayar pengacara terbaik. Itu sering terjadi.

lines.speaker: Steve
lines.text: One law for the rich, another for the poor. And that makes me angry, too!
lines.translation: Satu hukum untuk orang kaya, hukum lain untuk orang miskin. Dan itu juga membuat saya marah!

speakingLab.context: Simulasi diskusi tentang pendapat siswa terhadap sistem hukum dan keadilan sosial. Mr. Khoirul akan menanyakan pandanganmu tentang hukuman yang adil dan ketidaksetaraan dalam sistem peradilan

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Hi there! We've just read about some serious miscarriages of justice. What do you think - have you ever heard of a case where an innocent person went to prison?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, I have. In my country, there was a case where someone was wrongly convicted based on false witness testimony.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That's terrible. Now, thinking about the company director in our dialogue who got five years for stealing - do you think that's a fair sentence, or should white-collar criminals get harsher punishments?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I think five years is too lenient. Not only did he steal money, but he also destroyed people's livelihoods. Under no circumstances should someone who ruins 100 lives get such a light sentence.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Well said! You used negative inversion beautifully there. One more question - what do you think causes inequality in the justice system? Is it about money, education, or something else?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I believe it's mostly about money and access to good lawyers. Rarely can poor people afford the same legal defense as wealthy criminals.

quiz.question: Choose the correct negative inversion form: '_____ the case finished than the judge set them free.'
options: No sooner had
No sooner has
Never had
Not only had
quiz.explanation: Pola 'No sooner had + subject + past participle + than' digunakan untuk menyatakan dua kejadian yang terjadi berurutan sangat cepat. Setelah 'no sooner', gunakan 'had' (past perfect) karena kejadian pertama selesai sebelum kejadian kedua dimulai.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Under no circumstances _____ have committed such a terrible crime.'
options: could they
they could
did they
they did
quiz.explanation: Setelah 'under no circumstances' (dalam keadaan apapun tidak), gunakan inversi: modal verb + subject. Jadi urutannya 'could they', bukan 'they could'. Ini membuat kalimat terdengar sangat formal dan menekankan ketidakmungkinan.

quiz.question: Which legal term means 'to take back a confession that was given under pressure'?
options: to retract a confession
to appeal a verdict
to withhold evidence
to give evidence
quiz.explanation: 'To retract' artinya menarik kembali atau mencabut pernyataan. 'To retract a confession' berarti menarik kembali pengakuan, biasanya karena pengakuan tersebut dipaksa atau tidak benar. Ini yang terjadi pada kasus Guildford Four.

quiz.question: Rewrite in formal style with negative inversion: 'She had never seen such injustice before.'
options: Never had she seen such injustice before.
Never she had seen such injustice before.
She never had seen such injustice before.
Had never she seen such injustice before.
quiz.answer: Never had she seen such injustice before.
quiz.explanation: Ketika 'never' dipindah ke awal kalimat untuk penekanan, gunakan inversi: Never + had + subject + past participle. Urutannya menjadi 'Never had she seen', bukan 'Never she had seen'.

quiz.question: What does 'a miscarriage of justice' mean?
options: When an innocent person is wrongly convicted by the legal system
When a criminal escapes from prison
When a judge makes a small mistake in a trial
When a lawyer loses a case
quiz.answer: When an innocent person is wrongly convicted by the legal system
quiz.explanation: 'Miscarriage of justice' adalah istilah hukum yang merujuk pada kesalahan serius dalam sistem peradilan dimana orang yang tidak bersalah dinyatakan bersalah dan dihukum. Kasus Sally Clark, Rubin Carter, dan Guildford Four adalah contoh nyata miscarriage of justice.

quiz.question: Complete with correct inversion: '_____ did Carter and Artis not commit a murder, but they also had alibis.'
options: Not only
Never
Rarely
No sooner
quiz.explanation: Pola 'Not only... but also...' digunakan untuk menambahkan informasi kedua yang memperkuat informasi pertama. Setelah 'not only' di awal kalimat, gunakan inversi: auxiliary verb + subject. Jadi: 'Not only did Carter and Artis not commit...' (mereka tidak hanya tidak melakukan pembunuhan, tetapi mereka juga punya alibi).

modules.title: Unit 10: Learning for Life: Education, Memory & Nominalization
modules.objective: Mampu menggunakan pola reported speech (passive & active), menguasai kosakata pendidikan tinggi, dan berdiskusi tentang kebijakan pendidikan dengan argumentasi yang terstruktur.

theory.summary: Unit ini membahas cara melaporkan perkataan orang lain menggunakan reported verbs dan passive report structures. Kamu akan belajar pola seperti 'Experts think that...' atau 'It is believed that...', serta nominalisasi untuk membuat tulisan lebih formal. Materi ini penting untuk diskusi akademis dan penulisan esai tingkat lanjut.
rules: Reported verb patterns: Subject + reporting verb + that-clause (e.g., 'Experts think that more research is needed')
Passive report structures: It + passive verb + that-clause (e.g., 'It is believed that music helps memory')
Nominalization: Mengubah verb/adjective menjadi noun untuk tone formal (e.g., 'decide' → 'decision', 'expensive' → 'expense')
Hedging expressions: Menggunakan 'seem', 'appear', 'probably', 'are thought to' untuk menunjukkan kehati-hatian dalam klaim

commonTrap.trapTitle: Kesalahan Menggunakan Infinitive setelah Reporting Verbs
commonTrap.explanation: Banyak pemula salah menggunakan infinitive (to + verb) setelah reporting verbs seperti 'suggest', 'recommend', atau 'decide'. Padahal, kata-kata ini membutuhkan that-clause atau gerund, bukan infinitive.
commonTrap.wrong: The teacher suggested to study Physics instead of Drama.
commonTrap.correct: The teacher suggested studying Physics instead of Drama.

readinessQuestions.prompt: Manakah kalimat bahasa Inggris berikut yang menggunakan passive report structure (It + passive verb + that-clause) dengan benar?
options: It is believed that early childhood education significantly improves long-term academic outcomes.
Believed it is that early childhood education significantly improves long-term academic outcomes.
It believed that early childhood education significantly improves long-term academic outcomes.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Pola passive report structure yang benar adalah 'It + is/was + past participle + that-clause'. Opsi pertama mengikuti pola ini dengan tepat: 'It is believed that...'. Opsi kedua membalik susunan kata secara tidak gramatikal, dan opsi ketiga kehilangan kata kerja bantu 'is' yang wajib ada dalam konstruksi pasif.

readinessQuestions.prompt: Salah satu kesalahan umum adalah menggunakan infinitive (to + verb) setelah reporting verbs tertentu seperti 'suggest' atau 'recommend'. Manakah kalimat berikut yang menggunakan reporting verb dengan BENAR?
options: The professor suggested to postpone the dissertation deadline until next semester.
The professor recommended that students enrol in the advanced research module.
The professor recommended students to enrol in the advanced research module.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Kata kerja 'recommend' dan 'suggest' tidak diikuti oleh pola infinitive (to + verb). Pola yang benar adalah 'recommend/suggest + that-clause' atau 'recommend/suggest + gerund'. Opsi kedua menggunakan 'recommended that students enrol...' yang merupakan pola that-clause (subjunctive) yang tepat. Opsi pertama dan ketiga salah karena menggunakan infinitive setelah 'suggest' dan 'recommend'.

readinessQuestions.prompt:
Perhatikan percakapan berikut tentang keputusan pendidikan. Isilah bagian [...] dengan respons yang paling tepat dan natural.

Joanna: "Did they go to university? If not, what are they now doing?"
Harry: "What factors helped them make their decision?"
Tanya: "How do they feel now about the decision they made?"
Joanna: "I'd disagree. She sounds a bit selfish. [...]. He seems the most mature."
options: I'd rather talk to Harry
I'd suggest to talk to Harry
I'd prefer talk to Harry
readinessQuestions.explanation: Dalam konteks dialog ini, Joanna menyatakan preferensinya untuk berbicara dengan Harry. Pola yang benar adalah 'I'd rather + bare infinitive' (tanpa 'to'), yaitu 'I'd rather talk to Harry'. Opsi kedua salah karena 'suggest' tidak diikuti infinitive. Opsi ketiga salah karena 'prefer' membutuhkan 'to' sebelum kata kerja ('I'd prefer to talk'), bukan bare infinitive.

speakingLab.context: Mr. Khoirul meminta pendapatmu tentang kebijakan pendidikan tinggi dan apakah semua orang harus kuliah atau tidak.

turns.text: Do you think everyone should go to university, or are there good reasons not to? What's your view?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I think it depends on each person's goals. University is great for certain careers, but not everyone needs a degree to succeed.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul

turns.speaker: You

quiz.question: Complete the sentence with the correct reported verb pattern: 'The education minister _____ cutting at least one subject from the school curriculum.'
options: recommended
recommended to cut
recommended us cutting
quiz.explanation: Kata 'recommend' diikuti langsung oleh gerund (verb+ing) atau that-clause, bukan infinitive. Pola yang benar: 'recommended cutting' atau 'recommended that we cut'.

quiz.question: Which passive report structure is correct? 'Scientists ___ that music has beneficial effects on memory.'
options: are believing
believe
are believed
quiz.explanation: Dalam kalimat aktif dengan subject jelas (Scientists), gunakan simple present 'believe'. Passive structure 'It is believed that...' digunakan tanpa subject spesifik.

quiz.question: Choose the correct hedging expression: 'Playing music in hospital waiting rooms ___ patients' moods.'
options: definitely improves
improves
seems to improve
quiz.explanation: Hedging expression 'seems to' menunjukkan kehati-hatian dalam membuat klaim, cocok untuk konteks akademis. Ini lebih ilmiah daripada klaim absolut.

quiz.question: I was very lucky that I _____ a scholarship to do my master's degree.
options: won
took
went
quiz.explanation: Collocation yang tepat adalah 'won a scholarship' (memenangkan beasiswa). Kata 'took' digunakan untuk courses/exams, bukan scholarships.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct nominalization: 'After graduating, I want to do a postgrad course at Columbia University. It doesn't want to do his master's part-time, he wants to study full-time and finish within a year.' What's the noun form of 'graduate'?
options: graduation
graduating
graduate
quiz.explanation: Nominalisasi dari verb 'graduate' adalah noun 'graduation'. Ini digunakan untuk membuat kalimat lebih formal: 'After graduation' lebih formal dari 'After graduating'.

quiz.question: Which sentence uses the correct reporting verb pattern? 'The headteacher...'
options: Let's discuss this more before making a decision
suggested discussing the matter before deciding
suggested to discuss the issue first
quiz.answer: suggested discussing the matter before deciding
quiz.explanation: Verb 'suggest' harus diikuti gerund (verb+ing), bukan infinitive. Pola: 'suggest doing something' atau 'suggest that someone do something'.

modules.title: Unit 11: The Modern World: Society, Trends & Complex Syntax
modules.objective: Mampu menggunakan struktur pasif kompleks dan kausatif have dalam konteks modern, serta mendiskusikan tren sosial seperti kemarahan internet dan veganisme dengan ekspresi yang natural dan kritis

theory.summary: Unit ini membahas penggunaan struktur pasif lanjutan dan causative have untuk mengekspresikan situasi yang dialami atau dilakukan oleh orang lain. Selain itu, unit ini mengajarkan cara mengungkapkan pendapat tentang isu-isu kontemporer seperti internet rage, stres kehidupan modern, dan pilihan gaya hidup seperti veganisme dengan menggunakan kosakata sophisticated dan ekspresi akademis.
rules: Passive Voice (Lanjutan): Agent lebih mungkin dibagikan dalam passive daripada happy tone. Contoh: 'An angry post is more likely to be shared than a happy one.' Kita menggunakan passive ketika agen tidak penting atau sudah jelas.

Causative Have: Digunakan untuk menyatakan seseorang membuat orang lain melakukan sesuatu untuk mereka. Pola: Subject + have/get + object + past participle. Contoh: 'I try to have it delivered when I know I'll be in' (Saya mencoba meminta diantar saat saya di rumah). 'My car got broken into the other day' (Mobil saya dibobol tempo hari).

Modal Passives: Menggabungkan modal verb dengan struktur pasif. Pola: Modal + be + past participle. Contoh: 'Someone must be known' (Seseorang pasti dikenal). 'They believe that animals shouldn't be killed for our consumption' (Mereka percaya bahwa hewan seharusnya tidak dibunuh untuk konsumsi kita).

Suffix -ism untuk Ideology: Menambahkan -ism pada kata untuk membentuk kata benda yang menunjukkan ideologi atau sistem kepercayaan. Contoh: vegan → veganism, optimist → optimism, capital → capitalism, social → socialism.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Kesalahan Penggunaan Causative Have
commonTrap.explanation: Banyak pemula bingung membedakan antara 'have something done' (meminta orang lain melakukan sesuatu untuk kita) dengan 'have to do something' (harus melakukan sesuatu sendiri). Struktur causative have menunjukkan bahwa subjek tidak melakukan aksi tersebut sendiri, melainkan orang lain yang melakukan.
commonTrap.wrong: I had to repair my phone (berarti saya yang memperbaikinya sendiri)
commonTrap.correct: I had my phone repaired (berarti saya minta orang lain/teknisi memperbaikannya)

readinessQuestions.prompt: Manakah kalimat bahasa Inggris berikut yang menggunakan struktur causative have (meminta orang lain melakukan sesuatu untuk kita) dengan benar?
options: I had my laptop fixed by a technician last week.
I had to fix my laptop by myself last week.
I was having my laptop and fixed it last week.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Kalimat 'I had my laptop fixed by a technician' menggunakan pola causative have yang benar: Subject + had + object (my laptop) + past participle (fixed). Artinya, subjek meminta orang lain (teknisi) untuk memperbaiki laptopnya. Opsi kedua menggunakan 'had to fix' yang berarti 'harus memperbaiki sendiri', bukan causative. Opsi ketiga memiliki struktur yang salah secara gramatikal.

readinessQuestions.prompt: Perhatikan jebakan umum dalam penggunaan causative have. Jika seseorang ingin mengatakan bahwa ia meminta salon untuk memotong rambutnya, kalimat mana yang paling tepat?
options: I had to cut my hair at the salon yesterday.
I had my hair cut at the salon yesterday.
I have been cutting my hair at the salon yesterday.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Kalimat 'I had my hair cut at the salon' menggunakan causative have dengan benar (had + object + past participle), yang menunjukkan bahwa orang lain (penata rambut) yang memotong rambutnya. Opsi pertama 'had to cut' berarti 'harus memotong sendiri', yang merupakan jebakan umum. Opsi ketiga salah karena menggunakan present perfect continuous dengan 'yesterday', yang tidak sesuai secara tenses.

readinessQuestions.prompt:
Perhatikan percakapan berikut tentang kemarahan di internet dan keamanan digital. Lengkapi bagian yang kosong dengan respons yang paling natural dan sesuai konteks.

Emma: "Did you hear that radio show about internet rage? It's crazy how much anger there is online."
Jake: "Yeah, I know. I think people feel braver behind a screen."
Emma: "The host mentioned that most people only have one password. That's really risky, isn't it?"
Jake: "Definitely. [...] So I'm extra careful about security now."
options: My car got broken into the other day.
I have to break into my car the other day.
My car had been breaking the other day.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Kalimat 'My car got broken into the other day' adalah respons yang benar dan natural, menggunakan struktur pasif dengan 'get' (got + past participle) untuk menggambarkan pengalaman negatif yang terjadi pada mobilnya. Ini sesuai dengan konteks pembicaraan tentang keamanan. Opsi kedua salah karena 'have to break into my car' berarti 'harus membobol mobilku sendiri' dan penggunaan 'have to' dengan 'the other day' tidak cocok secara tenses. Opsi ketiga salah secara gramatikal karena 'had been breaking' tidak menyampaikan makna pasif yang tepat.

speakingLab.context: Anda sedang berdiskusi dengan Mr. Khoirul tentang pengalaman Anda dengan media sosial dan stres kehidupan modern. Latihan ini membantu Anda mengekspresikan pendapat tentang tren sosial kontemporer.

turns.text: Hi there! I'd like to hear your thoughts on social media. Do you think it makes people angrier, or does it just give angry people a platform?

turns.speaker: You

quiz.question: What does 'veganism' mean?

quiz.question: Which suffix is used to form words describing ideologies or belief systems?

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'My car _____ broken into the other day.'

quiz.question: If someone says one thing but does another, we can describe them as:
options: pessimistic
hypocritical
optimistic

modules.title: Unit 12: Celebrating Heroes: Mastery of Rhetoric, Nuance & Proficiency Exam
modules.objective: Mampu menggunakan future perfect dan future continuous untuk mengekspresikan antisipasi, serta menguasai kosakata tentang kesuksesan, kegagalan, dan penghargaan dalam konteks pahlawan kehidupan nyata.

theory.summary: Unit ini membahas penggunaan future perfect dan future continuous untuk membicarakan tindakan yang akan selesai atau sedang berlangsung di masa depan. Kita juga mempelajari cara mengungkapkan antisipasi dan membicarakan pahlawan kehidupan nyata dengan kosakata tentang penghargaan, kesuksesan, dan kegagalan.
rules: Future Perfect: 'will have + past participle' untuk tindakan yang akan selesai sebelum waktu tertentu di masa depan. Contoh: By the time I get home in the evening, I will have run several kilometres.

Future Continuous: 'will be + verb-ing' untuk tindakan yang akan sedang berlangsung pada waktu tertentu di masa depan. Contoh: In September, after I graduate, I will be helping out in Ghana to work in a hospital there.
Future in the Past: 'was/were going to' untuk rencana di masa lalu. Contoh: I was going to take them years to raise the money. He thought he was going to spend the rest of his life homeless.
Expressing anticipation: It's going to be amazing / I'm really looking forward to / I'm eagerly looking forward to / I can't wait to see

commonTrap.trapTitle: Kesalahan Penggunaan Future Perfect vs Future Continuous
commonTrap.explanation: Pemula sering bingung kapan menggunakan future perfect (untuk tindakan yang akan selesai) dan future continuous (untuk tindakan yang akan sedang berlangsung). Future perfect menekankan penyelesaian, sedangkan future continuous menekankan proses yang sedang terjadi.
commonTrap.wrong: By next week, I will be finishing the project.
commonTrap.correct: By next week, I will have finished the project. (menekankan penyelesaian)

readinessQuestions.prompt: Manakah kalimat bahasa Inggris berikut yang menggunakan future perfect dengan benar untuk menyatakan tindakan yang akan selesai sebelum waktu tertentu di masa depan?
options: By the time the ceremony begins, the committee will have nominated all the candidates.
By the time the ceremony begins, the committee will be nominating all the candidates.
By the time the ceremony begins, the committee will nominate all the candidates.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Kalimat pertama menggunakan future perfect ('will have nominated') dengan benar untuk menyatakan bahwa pencalonan semua kandidat akan sudah selesai sebelum upacara dimulai. Opsi kedua menggunakan future continuous yang menekankan proses sedang berlangsung, bukan penyelesaian. Opsi ketiga menggunakan simple future yang tidak menekankan bahwa tindakan akan selesai sebelum waktu tertentu.

readinessQuestions.prompt: Perhatikan perbedaan antara future perfect dan future continuous. Manakah kalimat yang paling tepat untuk menyatakan bahwa pada pukul 10 malam nanti, kamu masih dalam proses mengerjakan laporan (belum selesai)?
options: At 10 p.m. tonight, I will have worked on the report for the hero awards.
At 10 p.m. tonight, I will be working on the report for the hero awards.
At 10 p.m. tonight, I will have been working on the report for the hero awards.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Future continuous ('will be working') digunakan untuk menyatakan tindakan yang akan sedang berlangsung pada waktu tertentu di masa depan, artinya pada pukul 10 malam kamu masih dalam proses mengerjakan laporan. Opsi pertama (future perfect) menekankan penyelesaian, bukan proses. Opsi ketiga (future perfect continuous) menekankan durasi suatu aktivitas yang sudah berlangsung hingga titik waktu tertentu, bukan sekadar proses yang sedang terjadi saat itu.

readinessQuestions.prompt:
Perhatikan percakapan berikut. Jake dan Meg sedang dalam perjalanan bus menuju Brighton dan membicarakan rencana mereka. Isilah bagian [...] dengan ungkapan yang paling tepat dan natural.

Jake: "We should arrive by noon. [...] some fish and chips on the seafront!"
Meg: "Ha, that's right! I'm dying to have some ice cream, too."
options: I can't wait to have
I will have been eating
I was going to have had
readinessQuestions.explanation: Ungkapan 'I can't wait to have' adalah ekspresi antisipasi yang natural dan sesuai konteks percakapan santai tentang rencana makan di Brighton. Opsi kedua ('will have been eating') menggunakan future perfect continuous yang tidak sesuai konteks karena menyiratkan aktivitas yang sudah berlangsung lama. Opsi ketiga ('was going to have had') secara gramatikal janggal dan tidak natural dalam konteks percakapan ini.

lines.translation: Dan aku senang kita naik bus, bukan kereta: lebih murah, lebih nyaman, kamu bisa lihat pedesaan – tidak ada yang tidak disukai!

lines.speaker: Jake
lines.text: Me too. Remind me what time we get there! I'm absolutely starving. Let's go for some fish and chips, doesn't it?
lines.translation: Aku juga. Ingatkan aku jam berapa kita sampai di sana! Aku benar-benar lapar. Ayo makan fish and chips, bukankah begitu?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Ha, that's right! I'm dying to have some ice cream, too. But that'll have to wait until after our fish and chips – the bus is pulling over. Hang on, this is our stop. Why have we stopped just here?
lines.translation: Ha, benar! Aku sangat ingin makan es krim juga. Tapi itu harus menunggu setelah fish and chips kita – busnya sedang berhenti. Tunggu, ini perhentian kita. Kenapa kita berhenti di sini saja?

lines.speaker: Jake
lines.text: How should I know! Hang on, the driver's going to say something.
lines.translation: Mana aku tahu! Tunggu, sopirnya akan mengatakan sesuatu.

speakingLab.context: Mr. Khoirul sedang membantu Anda berlatih berbicara tentang rencana masa depan dan orang yang Anda kagumi sebagai pahlawan.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Hi there! I'd like to talk about people who inspire us. Can you think of someone you consider a hero in your life? It could be someone famous or someone you know personally.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Well, I really admire my grandmother. She raised six children by herself while running a small business. She never gave up despite all the challenges.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That's wonderful! What qualities does your grandmother have that make her heroic in your eyes? And how has she influenced your own goals?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: She's incredibly resilient and always puts others first. Because of her, I've decided to pursue a career in social work. By this time next year, I will have completed my training and I'll be helping families in need.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That's a beautiful goal! It sounds like you're really looking forward to making a difference. What do you think will be the most challenging part of your new career?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I think the emotional side will be tough. But I'm eagerly looking forward to the moment when I can actually help someone turn their life around, just like my grandmother did for our family.

quiz.question: By the end of next year, 2,000 young people from all over the world _____ the chance to live abroad and experience new cultures.
options: will have had
will be having
are going to have
will have
quiz.explanation: Gunakan future perfect (will have + past participle) untuk tindakan yang akan selesai sebelum waktu tertentu di masa depan. 'By the end of next year' menunjukkan waktu penyelesaian di masa depan.

quiz.question: In September, after I graduate, I _____ out in Ghana to work in a hospital there.
options: will be helping
will have helped
am helping
will help
quiz.explanation: Future continuous (will be + verb-ing) digunakan untuk tindakan yang akan sedang berlangsung pada waktu tertentu di masa depan. Konteksnya menunjukkan aktivitas yang akan berlangsung setelah lulus.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'future in the past'?
options: He thought he was going to spend the rest of his life homeless.
He thinks he will spend the rest of his life homeless.
He is going to spend the rest of his life homeless.
He will be spending the rest of his life homeless.
quiz.answer: He thought he was going to spend the rest of his life homeless.
quiz.explanation: 'Future in the past' menggunakan 'was/were going to' untuk mengungkapkan rencana atau ekspektasi di masa lalu. Kalimat ini menunjukkan apa yang dia pikirkan akan terjadi pada waktu itu.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase to express anticipation: 'I _____ to see what happens tomorrow!'
options: can't wait
don't wait
won't wait
wasn't waiting
quiz.explanation: 'Can't wait' adalah frasa yang tepat untuk mengekspresikan antisipasi atau kegembiraan tentang sesuatu yang akan terjadi. Ekspresi lain: 'I'm really looking forward to' atau 'I'm eagerly looking forward to'.

quiz.question: What does 'shortlist' mean in the context of awards?
options: To include someone in a final list of candidates
To write a short list
To reject someone from consideration
To make a list shorter by removing items
quiz.answer: To include someone in a final list of candidates
quiz.explanation: 'Shortlist' berarti memasukkan seseorang atau sesuatu dalam daftar pendek kandidat yang sudah dipilih dari banyak kandidat. Contoh: 'Mandy was shortlisted for the book award.'

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'They are _____ the running for the Teacher of the Year prize.'
options: in
on
at
for
quiz.explanation: Frasa yang benar adalah 'be in the running for something' yang berarti 'mempunyai peluang untuk memenangkan sesuatu'. Preposisi 'in' adalah bagian tetap dari frasa ini.

modules.title: Ujian Kelulusan C2.1: Evaluasi Komprehensif Mastery Foundations & Rhetoric
modules.objective: Ujian kelulusan komprehensif 4 keterampilan (Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking) untuk membuka Sub-Level C2.2

theory.summary: Ujian kelulusan C2.1 ini mengintegrasikan seluruh fondasi mastery yang telah Anda kuasai: nuansa habitual yang kompleks, psikologi naratif, kondisional lanjutan, struktur cleft dan inversi, serta kemampuan retoris tingkat tinggi. Di level C2, Anda tidak hanya memahami struktur gramatikal—Anda menguasai bagaimana memilih register, nada, dan konstruksi sintaksis yang tepat untuk menciptakan dampak persuasif maksimal. Ujian ini mensimulasikan situasi autentik Cambridge C2 Proficiency: mendengarkan monolog filosofis atau saintifik yang padat, membaca esai sastra atau teks hukum berlapis makna, menulis dengan presisi retoris, dan berbicara dengan kefasihan oratoris. Kelulusan membuktikan Anda siap memasuki C2.2 dengan kepercayaan diri seorang komunikator grandmaster.
rules: Inversion & Cleft untuk Penekanan Retoris: Gunakan inversi (Never have I witnessed..., Seldom does one encounter...) dan cleft structures (It is precisely this ambiguity that..., What concerns me most is...) untuk menggeser fokus informasi dan menciptakan efek dramatis atau persuasif dalam argumen kompleks.

Habitual & Iterative Nuances: Kuasai ekspresi kebiasaan lanjut (would invariably, used to unfailingly, was wont to) dan aspek iteratif (time and again, repeatedly) untuk menggambarkan pola perilaku dengan presisi temporal dan konotasi psikologis yang kaya.

Conditional Sophistication & Mixed Modality: Aplikasikan kondisional campuran (If she were to have known, she would never have consented) dan modalitas berlapis (It might well have been the case that..., One could scarcely have anticipated...) untuk menyampaikan hipotesis kontrafaktual dan epistemic uncertainty dengan kedalaman filosofis.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Peringatan Register dan Koherensi Pragmatik C2
commonTrap.explanation: Penutur C2 sejati tidak sekadar menggunakan struktur rumit—mereka memilih struktur yang koheren dengan konteks retoris dan audiens. Jebakan umum adalah overuse inversi atau cleft tanpa alasan pragmatik, yang membuat teks terasa artifisial atau bombastis. Begitu pula, penggunaan kondisional kompleks yang tidak diperlukan dapat mengaburkan makna alih-alih memperjelas. Di C2, less is more bila simplicity lebih elegan.
commonTrap.wrong: Rarely do I find myself in disagreement with such propositions, yet seldom have I encountered arguments so profoundly lacking in substantive merit.
commonTrap.correct: I rarely disagree with such propositions, yet I've seldom encountered arguments so lacking in substance.

readinessQuestions.prompt: Manakah kalimat bahasa Inggris berikut yang paling tepat menggunakan kombinasi inversi (inversion) dan cleft structure untuk penekanan retoris di level C2?
options: Never have I witnessed such a blatant disregard for due process, and it is precisely this negligence that undermines the integrity of the entire institution.
I have never witnessed such a blatant disregard for due process, and this negligence precisely undermines the integrity of the entire institution.
Never I have witnessed such a blatant disregard for due process, and it is precisely this negligence what undermines the integrity of the entire institution.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Opsi pertama benar karena menggunakan inversi dengan tepat ('Never have I witnessed...') diikuti auxiliary 'have' sebelum subjek 'I', serta cleft structure yang benar ('it is precisely this negligence that...'). Opsi kedua tidak menggunakan inversi maupun cleft. Opsi ketiga memiliki dua kesalahan: inversi yang salah ('Never I have' seharusnya 'Never have I') dan cleft yang salah ('this negligence what' seharusnya 'this negligence that').

readinessQuestions.prompt: Di level C2, penutur yang mahir harus menghindari penggunaan struktur kompleks secara berlebihan (overuse) yang justru membuat teks terasa artifisial. Manakah kalimat berikut yang paling tepat menerapkan prinsip koherensi pragmatik ini—menggunakan struktur canggih hanya ketika diperlukan?
options: Seldom does one find oneself in a position where rarely can it be said that never has such an argument been so profoundly devoid of merit.
The argument, while superficially compelling, is what one might call a textbook case of sophistry—it conflates correlation with causation at every turn.
It is the case that what must be said is that seldom has one encountered that which could scarcely have been anticipated to be so lacking in substance.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Opsi kedua benar karena menggunakan register tinggi secara natural dan proporsional tanpa menumpuk inversi atau cleft secara berlebihan. Opsi pertama dan ketiga menunjukkan jebakan umum C2: menumpuk beberapa inversi dan struktur kompleks dalam satu kalimat sehingga makna menjadi kabur dan terasa bombastis (artifisial), bukan elegan. Prinsip C2 adalah 'less is more'—pilih struktur canggih hanya bila konteks retoris menuntutnya.

readinessQuestions.prompt:
Perhatikan percakapan akademis berikut. Lengkapi bagian "[...]" dengan respons yang paling natural dan sesuai konteks.

Professor Ashworth: "Were these systems truly opaque, no perspicacious jurist would countenance their deployment."
Dr. Karimova: "[...]"
options: Ah, but therein lies the sophistry—equating technical explicability with moral intelligibility. The exigencies of judicial efficiency cannot exculpate us from our responsibility to preserve human judgment at the core of justice.
Yes, I completely agree with you. These systems are very good and we should use them more often because technology is always improving and getting better every day.
If these systems would have been opaque, I will not agree to use them, because the judges might not have been understanding how they are working properly.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Opsi pertama benar karena merespons argumen Professor Ashworth dengan counter-argument yang tajam dan koheren secara retoris, menggunakan register C2 yang tepat (sophistry, exigencies, exculpate). Opsi kedua terlalu sederhana dan tidak sesuai register akademis C2 dari percakapan ini. Opsi ketiga mengandung kesalahan kondisional campuran ('would have been... I will not agree') dan gramatikal ('might not have been understanding'), tidak mencerminkan kompetensi C2.

vocab.meaning: kebenaran yang tampak nyata; kemiripan dengan realitas; kredibilitas naratif
vocab.collocation: The novel's verisimilitude is compromised by anachronistic dialogue that betrays the author's lack of historical research.

vocab.meaning: sangat tajam dalam pemahaman; cerdik dan berpenglihatan jernih
vocab.collocation: Her perspicacious analysis of the geopolitical landscape allowed her to anticipate the crisis months before it unfolded.

vocab.meaning: kebutuhan mendesak; tuntutan situasi yang memerlukan tindakan segera
vocab.collocation: The exigencies of wartime governance often necessitate decisions that would be unconscionable in peacetime.

vocab.meaning: cercaan keras; penghinaan publik; reputasi buruk akibat kritik tajam
vocab.collocation: The whistleblower endured years of obloquy from former colleagues before vindication finally came.

vocab.meaning: argumen yang tampak meyakinkan namun sebenarnya keliru; penalaran menyesatkan
vocab.collocation: The minister's defence was nothing but sophistry, designed to obfuscate rather than illuminate the truth.

vocab.meaning: menenangkan atau meraih simpati pihak yang marah; meredakan kemarahan dengan pengorbanan
vocab.collocation: The corporation sought to propitiate environmental activists by pledging substantial investments in renewable energy.

vocab.meaning: sikap acuh tak acuh yang santai; ketidakpedulian yang tenang
vocab.collocation: His insouciance in the face of mounting criticism suggested either supreme confidence or dangerous delusion.

vocab.meaning: bersifat memihak atau bias; dirancang untuk mempromosikan sudut pandang tertentu
vocab.collocation: The documentary's tendentious editing presented a skewed narrative that ignored contradictory evidence.

vocab.meaning: membebaskan dari kesalahan atau tuduhan; membuktikan tidak bersalah
vocab.collocation: The forensic evidence served to exculpate the defendant, revealing egregious failures in the initial investigation.

vocab.meaning: sangat dalam dan sulit dipahami; tersembunyi dari pengetahuan umum; obscure
vocab.collocation: The philosopher's recondite arguments on modal metaphysics remain inaccessible to all but specialists in the field.

dialogue.context: Dialog akademis antara dua profesor filsafat yang memperdebatkan implikasi etis dari kecerdasan artifisial dalam pengambilan keputusan yudisial. Diskusi berlangsung setelah keynote presentation di konferensi internasional.

lines.speaker: Professor Ashworth
lines.text: Seldom have I encountered a proposition as philosophically tendentious as the claim that algorithmic adjudication can possess moral agency.
lines.translation: Jarang saya menemukan proposisi yang secara filosofis begitu bias seperti klaim bahwa putusan algoritmik dapat memiliki agensi moral.

lines.speaker: Dr. Karimova
lines.text: Yet what concerns me most is not the agency itself, but rather the insouciance with which we delegate life-altering decisions to systems whose epistemological foundations remain fundamentally recondite.
lines.translation: Namun yang paling mengkhawatirkan saya bukanlah agensi itu sendiri, melainkan sikap acuh tak acuh di mana kita mendelegasikan keputusan yang mengubah hidup kepada sistem yang fondasi epistemologisnya tetap sangat sulit dipahami.

lines.speaker: Professor Ashworth
lines.text: I would argue, with all due respect, that your characterisation betrays a certain misconception. Were these systems truly opaque, no perspicacious jurist would countenance their deployment.
lines.translation: Saya berpendapat, dengan segala hormat, bahwa karakterisasi Anda mengkhianati kesalahpahaman tertentu. Seandainya sistem-sistem ini benar-benar tidak transparan, tak ada yuris yang cerdik akan menyetujui penerapannya.

lines.speaker: Dr. Karimova
lines.text: Ah, but therein lies the sophistry—equating technical explicability with moral intelligibility. The exigencies of judicial efficiency cannot exculpate us from our responsibility to preserve human judgment at the core of justice.
lines.translation: Ah, tetapi di situlah letak penalaran sesat itu—menyamakan penjelasan teknis dengan pemahaman moral. Kebutuhan mendesak akan efisiensi yudisial tidak dapat membebaskan kita dari tanggung jawab untuk mempertahankan penilaian manusia sebagai inti keadilan.

lines.speaker: Professor Ashworth
lines.text: Rarely do I concede a point mid-debate, yet you've identified precisely the lacuna in my argument. It is the verisimilitude of neutrality, not neutrality itself, that algorithms offer.
lines.translation: Jarang saya mengakui sebuah poin di tengah perdebatan, namun Anda telah mengidentifikasi dengan tepat kekosongan dalam argumen saya. Ini adalah penampakan netralitas, bukan netralitas itu sendiri, yang ditawarkan algoritma.

lines.speaker: Dr. Karimova
lines.text: Indeed. And might we not argue that the obloquy directed at human judges for their fallibility is itself unjust, given that algorithms merely encode societal biases with greater efficiency?
lines.translation: Memang. Dan bukankah kita dapat berargumen bahwa cercaan yang ditujukan kepada hakim manusia atas ketidaksempurnaan mereka adalah tidak adil, mengingat algoritma hanya mengkodekan bias masyarakat dengan efisiensi yang lebih besar?

lines.speaker: Professor Ashworth
lines.text: Your analogy is apt. What we require, then, is not the displacement of human judgment, but rather its augmentation—a hybrid model that propitates both efficiency and ethical oversight.
lines.translation: Analogi Anda tepat. Yang kita perlukan, kalau begitu, bukanlah penggantian penilaian manusia, melainkan penguatannya—model hibrid yang meraih baik efisiensi maupun pengawasan etis.

lines.speaker: Dr. Karimova
lines.text: Precisely. Never have the stakes been higher, yet seldom have we been better positioned to forge a path that honours both innovation and our enduring commitment to justice.
lines.translation: Tepat sekali. Tidak pernah taruhannya setinggi ini, namun jarang kita berada dalam posisi yang lebih baik untuk menempa jalan yang menghormati baik inovasi maupun komitmen abadi kita pada keadilan.

speakingLab.context: Mr. Khoirul berperan sebagai moderator panel diskusi tingkat Cambridge C2 Proficiency. Anda adalah salah satu panelist yang harus menyampaikan pandangan persuasif tentang dampak teknologi terhadap privasi individual, kemudian merespons pertanyaan kritis dari moderator. Gunakan inversi, cleft structures, dan modalitas kompleks untuk mendemonstrasikan kefasihan grandmaster.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Good evening, and welcome to our panel discussion on the ethical dimensions of surveillance capitalism. Let me begin by inviting our first panelist to share their opening statement. What is your position on the balance between technological innovation and individual privacy?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. Rarely have we faced a technological paradigm so fundamentally at odds with the principles of liberal democracy. What concerns me most is not merely the erosion of privacy, but the insouciance with which society has accepted this erosion as inevitable.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: A provocative opening. But surely you would concede that individuals willingly consent to data collection in exchange for services? How do you reconcile personal agency with your claims of systemic coercion?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I would argue that the notion of informed consent is itself a sophistry in this context. Were users truly cognisant of the implications, one could scarcely imagine such widespread acquiescence. It is the verisimilitude of choice, not genuine choice, that platforms engineer.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Interesting. Let me press you further: what regulatory framework would you propose that doesn't stifle innovation while protecting fundamental rights? The exigencies of global competitiveness make this a particularly thorny question.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Indeed, and it is precisely this false dichotomy that I challenge. Never have we been forced to choose between innovation and ethics—that framing serves corporate interests, not public welfare. What we require is a perspicacious regulatory regime that recognises data dignity as foundational, not negotiable.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: A compelling vision, though some would characterise it as idealistic. How do you respond to critics who suggest that such regulation would drive technology companies to less scrupulous jurisdictions?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: That argument, with respect, is tendentious fearmongering. The EU's GDPR demonstrates that robust protection can coexist with a thriving digital economy. Seldom do we hear advocates of regulatory minimalism acknowledge that unchecked data exploitation imposes costs—social, psychological, political—that far exceed any efficiency gains.

quiz.question: [Listening Comprehension] You hear a philosophy professor delivering a lecture on epistemology: 'Never in the history of Western thought have we witnessed such a radical departure from foundationalist theories of knowledge. What concerns us today is not whether justified true belief constitutes knowledge, but whether the very concept of justification remains tenable in a post-truth era.' What is the speaker's primary concern? ___
options: The historical evolution of epistemological theories
The viability of justification as an epistemic concept in contemporary discourse
The definition of knowledge as justified true belief
quiz.answer: The viability of justification as an epistemic concept in contemporary discourse
quiz.explanation: Pembicara menggunakan cleft structure 'What concerns us today is...' untuk menekankan fokus utama: bukan definisi pengetahuan itu sendiri, tetapi apakah konsep justifikasi masih dapat dipertahankan di era pasca-kebenaran. Pilihan ini menangkap kekhawatiran epistemik kontemporer yang digarisbawahi pembicara, bukan sekadar survei historis atau definisi klasik.

quiz.question: [Listening Comprehension] In the same lecture, the professor continues: 'Seldom do we encounter arguments as perspicacious as those advanced by virtue epistemologists, yet rarely have I witnessed such widespread resistance to their insights among analytic philosophers.' What does the speaker imply about virtue epistemology? ___
options: It is widely accepted in analytic philosophy circles
It offers sharp insights but faces significant opposition within analytic tradition
It lacks the perspicacity of other epistemological approaches
quiz.answer: It offers sharp insights but faces significant opposition within analytic tradition
quiz.explanation: Inversi ganda ('Seldom... yet rarely...') menciptakan kontras retoris: pembicara mengakui ketajaman (perspicacious) argumen virtue epistemology sambil mencatat resistensi luas di kalangan filsuf analitik. Struktur ini mengungkapkan apresiasi yang dikombinasikan dengan kritik terhadap penerimaan terbatas—bukan penerimaan luas atau kurangnya kualitas.

quiz.question: [Listening Comprehension] A scientist discusses climate modelling: 'It might well have been the case that early projections underestimated warming rates, yet what remains incontrovertible is the anthropogenic causation. One could scarcely have anticipated the rapidity with which Arctic ice shelves would destabilise.' What epistemic stance does the speaker adopt regarding early climate projections? ___
options: Certainty that early projections were accurate
Acknowledgment of potential underestimation while affirming human causation
Scepticism about anthropogenic climate change
quiz.answer: Acknowledgment of potential underestimation while affirming human causation
quiz.explanation: Modalitas kompleks 'might well have been' mengindikasikan kemungkinan (bukan kepastian) bahwa proyeksi awal meremehkan laju pemanasan, sementara 'what remains incontrovertible' adalah cleft structure yang menekankan kepastian mutlak tentang penyebab antropogenik. Pembicara menyeimbangkan ketidakpastian tentang detail proyeksi dengan keyakinan kuat tentang kausalitas manusia.

quiz.question: [Listening Comprehension] A legal scholar discusses judicial precedent: 'Were the Court to have applied strict constructionism, the outcome would have differed markedly. Rarely does a single ruling carry such far-reaching implications for substantive due process.' What does the speaker suggest about the Court's actual approach? ___
options: The Court applied strict constructionism
The Court did not apply strict constructionism, resulting in significant due process implications
Strict constructionism would have had no impact on the outcome
quiz.answer: The Court did not apply strict constructionism, resulting in significant due process implications
quiz.explanation: Kondisional kontrafaktual past perfect ('Were the Court to have applied...') mengindikasikan bahwa Pengadilan TIDAK menerapkan strict constructionism—ini adalah hipotesis bertentangan dengan fakta. Inversi 'Rarely does...' kemudian menekankan dampak luas dari putusan aktual, yang didasarkan pada pendekatan yang lebih liberal terhadap interpretasi konstitusional.

quiz.question: [Reading Comprehension] Read this passage from a literary essay: 'The novel's verisimilitude is undermined not by fantastical elements per se, but by the author's tendency toward tendentious characterisation. What one expects from realist fiction is not empirical accuracy, but rather psychological plausibility—a quality conspicuously absent here.' The critic's main objection is that the novel ___.
options: Contains too many fantastical elements that break immersion
Lacks psychological credibility due to biased character portrayals
Fails to achieve empirical accuracy in depicting reality
quiz.answer: Lacks psychological credibility due to biased character portrayals
quiz.explanation: Kritikus menggunakan cleft structure 'What one expects... is not... but rather...' untuk membedakan akurasi empiris (yang tidak masalah) dari plausibilitas psikologis (yang kurang). 'Tendentious characterisation' merujuk pada penggambaran karakter yang bias atau berat sebelah, yang merusak kredibilitas psikologis—bukan elemen fantasi atau ketidakakuratan faktual.

quiz.question: [Reading Comprehension] The essay continues: 'Seldom have I encountered prose so exquisitely wrought yet so utterly devoid of genuine insight. The author's perspicacious observations on class dynamics cannot exculpate the work's fundamental lack of narrative coherence.' What is the critic's overall assessment? ___
options: The prose quality and social insights fully compensate for structural weaknesses
Despite elegant prose and sharp social observation, the work fails due to incoherent narrative structure
The author lacks perspicacity in analysing class dynamics
quiz.answer: Despite elegant prose and sharp social observation, the work fails due to incoherent narrative structure
quiz.explanation: Inversi 'Seldom have I...' mengakui keindahan prosa yang luar biasa, dan 'perspicacious observations' mengakui ketajaman analisis sosial, namun 'cannot exculpate' (tidak dapat membebaskan dari kesalahan) menunjukkan bahwa kualitas-kualitas ini tidak cukup mengatasi kekurangan koherensi naratif yang mendasar. Ini adalah penilaian bercampur yang pada akhirnya negatif.

quiz.question: [Reading Comprehension] From a legal opinion: 'The defendant's insouciance regarding fiduciary responsibilities constitutes not mere negligence but wilful malfeasance. Never has this Court witnessed such flagrant disregard for shareholder interests, nor have we encountered sophistry so transparently designed to obfuscate criminal intent.' The Court characterises the defendant's behaviour as ___.
options: Negligent but not intentionally criminal
Deliberately wrongful with attempts to conceal criminal purpose through misleading arguments
Merely careless in handling fiduciary duties
quiz.answer: Deliberately wrongful with attempts to conceal criminal purpose through misleading arguments
quiz.explanation: Pengadilan secara eksplisit menolak 'mere negligence' dan menegaskan 'wilful malfeasance' (kesalahan yang disengaja). 'Insouciance' (sikap acuh tak acuh) disebut dalam konteks tanggung jawab fidusia, dan 'sophistry... designed to obfuscate criminal intent' menunjukkan upuran sengaja untuk menyembunyikan niat kriminal melalui argumen menyesatkan—bukan sekadar kelalaian.

quiz.question: [Reading Comprehension] A philosophical text states: 'One could scarcely have anticipated the obloquy that would be heaped upon consequentialist ethics following the publication of Williams's critique. What remains recondite to most readers is the subtlety of his objection—not to outcomes as morally relevant, but to their sufficiency as the sole basis for ethical evaluation.' Williams's critique primarily challenges ___.
options: The relevance of outcomes in moral assessment
The adequacy of outcomes alone as the complete foundation of ethical judgment
The subtlety and accessibility of consequentialist reasoning
quiz.answer: The adequacy of outcomes alone as the complete foundation of ethical judgment
quiz.explanation: Cleft structure 'What remains recondite... is the subtlety of his objection' menekankan bahwa kebanyakan pembaca melewatkan nuansa: Williams TIDAK menolak bahwa outcomes itu relevan secara moral ('not to outcomes as morally relevant'), tetapi menantang 'their sufficiency as the sole basis'—bahwa hasil saja tidak cukup sebagai satu-satunya dasar penilaian etis. Ini adalah kritik terhadap kecukupan, bukan relevansi.

quiz.question: [Writing & Grammar] Which sentence demonstrates the most sophisticated use of inversion to emphasise the unprecedented nature of a scientific discovery? ___
options: We have never before witnessed such a radical departure from established quantum theory.
Never before have we witnessed such a radical departure from established quantum theory.
Such a radical departure from established quantum theory has never been witnessed before by us.
quiz.answer: Never before have we witnessed such a radical departure from established quantum theory.
quiz.explanation: Inversi dengan negative adverbial di awal kalimat ('Never before have we...') menciptakan penekanan dramatis dan register formal yang sesuai dengan konteks ilmiah C2. Pilihan pertama adalah struktur standar yang kurang berdampak retoris, sementara pilihan ketiga dengan passive voice dan 'by us' di akhir terasa kaku dan tidak natural untuk konteks ini.

quiz.question: [Writing & Grammar] Select the sentence that most effectively uses a cleft structure to highlight the specific concern in an ethical debate: ___
options: The algorithm's opacity concerns me most in this debate about AI ethics.
What concerns me most in this debate about AI ethics is the algorithm's opacity.
In this debate about AI ethics, I am most concerned by the algorithm's opacity.
quiz.answer: What concerns me most in this debate about AI ethics is the algorithm's opacity.
quiz.explanation: Cleft structure dengan 'What... is...' memungkinkan pembicara untuk memposisikan 'the algorithm's opacity' di akhir kalimat sebagai fokus informasi baru (rheme), menciptakan penekanan retoris yang kuat. Struktur ini juga memberikan bobot formal yang sesuai untuk debat etika tingkat tinggi. Pilihan lain kurang efektif dalam menciptakan penekanan topik-komentar yang diinginkan di level C2.

quiz.question: [Writing & Grammar] Which conditional construction most accurately expresses a complex counterfactual scenario with epistemic nuance? ___
options: If the government would have implemented stricter regulations, the crisis might have been prevented.
Had the government implemented stricter regulations, the crisis might well have been averted.
If the government had implemented stricter regulations, the crisis would definitely have been prevented.
quiz.answer: Had the government implemented stricter regulations, the crisis might well have been averted.
quiz.explanation: Inversi kondisional ('Had the government...') dengan modalitas epistemik 'might well have' mengekspresikan kemungkinan kuat (tetapi bukan kepastian) dalam skenario kontrafaktual—ini adalah nuansa C2 yang canggih. Pilihan pertama menggunakan 'would have' yang tidak gramatikal dalam if-clause. Pilihan ketiga dengan 'would definitely' terlalu kategoris dan kehilangan nuansa epistemik yang diperlukan untuk klaim kausal kompleks.

quiz.question: [Writing & Grammar] Identify the sentence that best demonstrates sophisticated use of relative clauses to create a complex, layered argument: ___
options: The policy, which many economists criticised, failed to address inequality.
The policy, which many economists whose models predicted inflation criticised, failed to address the structural inequality that had precipitated the crisis.
The policy failed to address inequality, and many economists criticised it.
quiz.answer: The policy, which many economists whose models predicted inflation criticised, failed to address the structural inequality that had precipitated the crisis.
quiz.explanation: Kalimat ini menggunakan relative clause bertingkat ('economists whose models predicted inflation') dan additional relative clause ('inequality that had precipitated') untuk menciptakan argumen berlapis dengan kepadatan informasi tinggi—karakteristik prosa akademis C2. Kalimat ini menunjukkan kemampuan untuk mengintegrasikan multiple propositions secara koheren dalam satu struktur sintaksis yang kompleks namun masih dapat dipahami.

quiz.question: [Speaking & Situational Dialogue] You are responding to a critic who challenges your position on immigration policy. Which response demonstrates the most effective use of C2 rhetorical strategies to rebut while maintaining diplomatic register? ___
options: I think you're wrong about that, and here's why: immigration actually benefits the economy.
Your argument is completely flawed and ignores all the economic evidence supporting immigration.

Rarely do I encounter an argument that so fundamentally misconstrues the economic evidence. What you characterise as fiscal burden is, upon closer examination, precisely the demographic dividend that sustains our social safety net.
quiz.answer: Rarely do I encounter an argument that so fundamentally misconstrues the economic evidence. What you characterise as fiscal burden is, upon closer examination, precisely the demographic dividend that sustains our social safety net.
quiz.explanation: Respons ini menggunakan inversi ('Rarely do I...') untuk menyampaikan ketidaksetujuan kuat dengan register formal yang diplomatik, lalu menggunakan cleft structure ('What you characterise...') untuk secara langsung mengkonfrontasi dan mereframe argumen lawan. Ini adalah strategi retoris C2: tegas dalam substansi, elegan dalam penyampaian, dengan menghindari serangan ad hominem atau bahasa konfrontatif yang kasar.

quiz.question: [Speaking & Situational Dialogue] In a keynote address, you need to transition from acknowledging a problem to proposing a solution. Which transition demonstrates grandmaster-level rhetorical sophistication? ___
options: So now that we've talked about the problem, let me tell you about my solution.
Having identified these challenges, I now turn to potential solutions.
Seldom have the challenges been so formidable, yet never have we been better positioned to forge solutions that honour both pragmatic constraints and our deepest ethical commitments.
quiz.answer: Seldom have the challenges been so formidable, yet never have we been better positioned to forge solutions that honour both pragmatic constraints and our deepest ethical commitments.
quiz.explanation: Transisi ini menggunakan inversi paralel ('Seldom... yet never...') untuk menciptakan kontras retoris yang powerful antara skala tantangan dan potensi solusi, sambil mengartikulasikan komitmen ganda terhadap pragmatisme dan etika—ini adalah oratory tingkat tinggi yang menginspirasi tanpa terdengar naif. Pilihan lain terlalu prosaic atau transaksional untuk keynote C2.

quiz.question: [Speaking & Situational Dialogue] You must diplomatically disagree with a senior colleague in a public forum. Which formulation achieves disagreement while preserving face and demonstrating epistemic humility? ___
options: I'm afraid I have to disagree with your analysis completely.
With all due respect, your conclusions are not supported by the data.

I would venture to suggest, with considerable deference to your expertise, that the data might admit of an alternative interpretation—one which, were we to adopt it, could well reconcile the apparent contradictions you've identified.
quiz.answer: I would venture to suggest, with considerable deference to your expertise, that the data might admit of an alternative interpretation—one which, were we to adopt it, could well reconcile the apparent contradictions you've identified.
quiz.explanation: Formulasi ini mendemonstrasikan diplomasi C2 melalui multiple hedging devices ('would venture,' 'might admit of,' 'could well'), explicit deference, dan kondisional yang membingkai alternatif sebagai kemungkinan rekonsiliasi alih-alih konflik langsung. Ini adalah disagreement yang konstruktif dan sophisticate, yang mempertahankan muka kedua belah pihak sambil tetap menyampaikan substansi intelektual—esensial untuk discourse akademis atau profesional tingkat tinggi.

quiz.question: [Speaking & Situational Dialogue] In responding to a provocative question from the audience, which answer demonstrates the ability to reframe the question while addressing its underlying concern? ___
options: That's not really the right question to ask in this context.
Let me answer your question directly: yes, I believe the policy would work.

What you're asking, if I understand correctly, is not whether the policy is politically feasible—though that matters—but whether it can be morally justified. And it's precisely that ethical dimension that I wish to foreground, because rarely do we acknowledge that feasibility arguments often serve to foreclose ethical deliberation prematurely.
quiz.answer: What you're asking, if I understand correctly, is not whether the policy is politically feasible—though that matters—but whether it can be morally justified. And it's precisely that ethical dimension that I wish to foreground, because rarely do we acknowledge that feasibility arguments often serve to foreclose ethical deliberation prematurely.
quiz.explanation: Respons ini mendemonstrasikan active listening melalui 'if I understand correctly,' kemudian menggunakan cleft structure untuk reframe pertanyaan dari feasibilitas politik ke justifikasi moral—sebuah reframing yang sophisticate dan substantif. Inversi 'rarely do we acknowledge' kemudian mengangkat meta-kritik tentang bagaimana argumen feasibilitas sering menutup debat etika. Ini adalah C2 mastery: mengelola dialog dengan menggeser frame diskusi sambil tetap respectful terhadap penanya.

modules.title: Nuanced Satire, Irony & High-Level Rhetorical Sarcasm in Cultural Commentary
modules.objective: Menganalisis dan menyusun kritik sosial bernada satir, sarkasme terselubung, parodi sastra, dan humor intelektual.

theory.summary: Satir tingkat C2 merupakan seni retorika tertinggi yang mengkritik absurditas sosial, politik, atau budaya melalui ironi berlapis, sarkasme terselubung, dan parodi intelektual. Berbeda dengan ejekan kasar, satir mahir menggunakan understatement, hiperbola terkendali, dan ambiguitas sengaja untuk memaksa pembaca menemukan makna tersembunyi. Teknik Swiftian irony menciptakan jarak antara permukaan teks dan maksud sebenarnya, sementara deadpan commentary menyampaikan kritik tajam dengan nada datar yang kontras dengan isinya. Penutur C2 mampu memparodikan gaya sastra, menggunakan lampoon untuk mengekspos kemunafikan, dan menyusun cultural subversion yang menggugat hegemoni wacana dominan—semuanya dengan presisi linguistik dan kesadaran pragmatik yang sempurna.
rules: Gunakan dramatic irony dengan sengaja menciptakan kesenjangan antara apa yang dikatakan dan apa yang dimaksud, seringkali melalui persona naif atau overstatement yang absurd untuk mengekspos kontradiksi sistemik
Terapkan Socratic irony dengan berpura-pura tidak tahu atau merendahkan diri untuk memancing lawan bicara mengungkap kebodohan atau arogansinya sendiri, teknik ini efektif dalam debat intelektual

Kombinasikan bathos (penurunan tiba-tiba dari bahasa mulia ke trivial) dengan zeugma (satu kata mengatur dua frasa dengan makna berbeda) untuk menciptakan efek komikal yang sekaligus menusuk: 'She lost her reputation and her umbrella'—struktur paralel yang kontras semantik

commonTrap.trapTitle: Peringatan Nuansa dan Ketepatan Pragmatik C2
commonTrap.explanation: Satir gagal bukan karena kurang tajam, melainkan karena terlalu eksplisit atau kehilangan ambiguitas produktif. Penutur C1 cenderung menjelaskan leluconnya atau menggunakan penanda ironi yang terlalu jelas ('obviously', 'of course'). Penutur C2 memahami bahwa kekuatan satir terletak pada ketegangan interpretif—pembaca harus bekerja untuk menemukan makna, dan dalam proses itu, kritik menjadi lebih menancap. Register juga krusial: satir aristokratik berbeda dengan satir populis, dan memilih register yang salah menghancurkan efek retoris.
commonTrap.wrong: The politician's promises are obviously lies and everyone knows he's corrupt, which is clearly ridiculous.
commonTrap.correct: One admires the politician's unwavering commitment to principles—particularly the principle that today's convictions need not constrain tomorrow's opportunities.

readinessQuestions.prompt: Manakah kalimat bahasa Inggris berikut yang paling tepat menerapkan teknik satir tingkat tinggi (C2) dengan menggunakan ironi terselubung dan ambiguitas produktif untuk mengkritik suatu fenomena sosial?
options: The committee's dedication to transparency is truly inspiring—one notes how every critical document is released at 5 p.m. on a Friday before a holiday weekend.
The committee is totally corrupt and they hide everything from the public, which is absolutely disgusting and everyone should be outraged.
The committee sometimes lacks transparency, and perhaps they could improve their communication strategies going forward.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Opsi pertama menggunakan ironi terselubung khas C2: pujian di permukaan ('dedication to transparency is truly inspiring') yang kontras dengan fakta spesifik yang mengekspos kemunafikan (merilis dokumen di waktu yang tidak akan dibaca siapa pun). Opsi kedua terlalu eksplisit dan kehilangan ambiguitas produktif—ini bukan satir melainkan cercaan langsung. Opsi ketiga hanyalah kritik netral biasa tanpa unsur ironi atau satir sama sekali.

readinessQuestions.prompt: Salah satu jebakan umum dalam satir C2 adalah penggunaan penanda ironi yang terlalu eksplisit (seperti 'obviously', 'clearly', 'of course') sehingga menghancurkan ketegangan interpretif. Manakah kalimat berikut yang berhasil menghindari jebakan ini dan mempertahankan kekuatan satir melalui ambiguitas yang produktif?
options: The CEO's environmental pledge is obviously just greenwashing, and of course nobody actually believes his clearly performative gestures.
One applauds the CEO's environmental pledge—a bold initiative that, by remarkable coincidence, was announced the same week as the EPA investigation.
The CEO is clearly lying about caring for the environment, which is obviously hypocritical given his company's pollution record.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Opsi kedua adalah satir C2 yang efektif karena tidak menggunakan penanda ironi eksplisit ('obviously', 'clearly', 'of course'). Kritiknya disampaikan melalui juxtaposition fakta ('bold initiative' bertepatan dengan 'EPA investigation') yang membiarkan pembaca sendiri menarik kesimpulan. Opsi pertama dan ketiga sama-sama gagal karena dipenuhi penanda ironi eksplisit yang menghancurkan ambiguitas produktif—ciri khas penutur C1 yang belum menguasai kehalusan satir.

readinessQuestions.prompt:
Perhatikan percakapan satir berikut antara dua akademisi yang sedang mendiskusikan sebuah novel. Isilah bagian [...] dengan respons yang paling tepat secara kontekstual dan sesuai dengan nada sarkasme intelektual yang digunakan dalam percakapan:

Dr. Hartwick: "The critics have been remarkably generous, though I suspect their enthusiasm correlates rather precisely with the publisher's advertising budget."

Prof. Desai: "[...]"
options: That's a really mean thing to say. The critics are professionals and they would never let advertising influence their reviews.
How cynical of you. Surely you don't mean to suggest that literary merit can be manufactured through strategic placement in the Sunday supplements?
Yes, I agree completely. The publishing industry is corrupt and critics are all paid shills who cannot be trusted.
